conventions.convention: The real spaces have integer dimensions 1 ≤ r ≤ n. Stiefel uses the induced Frobenius metric; Grassmann uses the quotient metric with horizontal representatives satisfying XᵀZ=0. Frame changes act simultaneously by (X,Z) ↦ (XQ,ZQ), Q orthogonal.
Complex matrix spaces are real vector spaces with inner product Re tr(U*V). Complex Grassmann uses the right unitary quotient and horizontal representatives X*Z=0.
The QR factor has positive diagonal in its upper-triangular factor. QR and polar formulas are exact-arithmetic maps. Their Grassmann outputs are column spaces; QR frame equivariance is not assumed.
Representative-based Grassmann vector transport uses the polar endpoint and horizontal source vectors. Stiefel transport may use either QR or polar endpoints.
Armijo tests t_j=β^j for j=0,…,J, including J=0. A zero gradient returns stationary; exhausting unsuccessful trials returns budget-exhausted.

Trust-region tangent spaces and model operators are real. Operator norm is zero on a zero tangent space. Zero-denominator radius thresholds are infinite. Failed or inadequate subproblem candidates use the Cauchy fallback; small radii force that fallback. Gradient and target checks precede the outer-cap check.

The trust-region complexity target satisfies 0<ε≤1. Counts include accepted and rejected outer trials, with available model/objective evaluations and a sufficiently large outer cap; they do not bound inner subproblem operations.

load_bearing.statement: For X∈St(n,r), T_X St(n,r)={Z:XᵀZ+ZᵀX=0}, and its Frobenius orthogonal projection is G−X sym(XᵀG). Grassmann tangent vectors at [X] have unique horizontal representatives XᵀZ=0, with horizontal projection (I−XXᵀ)G.

On the full-column-rank domains of def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions, the positive-diagonal QR and polar maps are smooth, take values in St(n,r), fix η=0, and have differential DR_X(0)[η]=η. Their induced Grassmann maps are representative-independent and have identity differential under the horizontal tangent identification. No second-order claim is made.

For X∈St_C(n,r), as a real manifold, T_X St_C(n,r)={Z:X*Z+Z*X=0}, and its orthogonal projection is G−X Herm(X*G). The complex Grassmann tangent has unique horizontal representatives X*Z=0, with projection (I−XX*)G.

The frame formula of def-complex-grassmann-polar-retraction is smooth on the horizontal tangent bundle, maps into St_C(n,r), fixes zero, and has frame differential DR_X(0)[η]=η for horizontal η. It is right-unitary equivariant, and its range map is a representative-independent first-order retraction on Gr_C(r,n).

For F smooth on an open neighborhood of St(n,r), with G=∇F(X), its Stiefel restriction has gradient G−X sym(XᵀG). If F(XQ)=F(X) for every orthogonal Q, it descends to a smooth Grassmann objective with horizontal gradient (I−XXᵀ)G. In either metric, gradient zero is equivalent to criticality of the restricted objective.

For 1≤r≤n, let E be real-valued and continuously differentiable on an open set of Hermitian matrices containing the rank-r orthogonal projectors. If its Hermitian real Frobenius gradient K(P) satisfies DE(P)[H]=Re tr(K(P)*H) for every Hermitian H, then f([X])=E(XX*) is well-defined and has horizontal gradient 2(I−XX*)K(XX*)X.

Coordinate interpretation of Frobenius pairings and positivity.
Compactness of nonempty closed bounded real-coordinate frame sets.

Equivalence of criticality and a vanishing projected gradient.

Smooth inverse-root factors, including inversion after realification.
Reduced QR conventions.
Construction and smooth recurrence of positive-diagonal QR on full-rank matrices.
Diagonalization of real positive-definite Gram matrices.
Operator bounds in orthonormal real tangent coordinates.
Pullback differential, model-curvature, and ratio-error estimates.

Attained objective minima on compact frame sets, followed by quotient surjectivity.
Positive-radius logarithms in rejected-trial counting.
Telescoping multiplicative radius updates and monotonicity.
Choosing a finite accepted-step count exceeding the available objective-decrease budget.
Excluding infinitely many consecutive rejections at a fixed nonstationary point.
